The reason there's no incentive for them to upgrade infrastructure now is because ISPs intentionally overlap their service areas just enough to skirt monopoly laws. Most people would consider you lucky if you had a choice between internet providers. I don't see how getting rid of net neutrality, such as it is, would help that. Another implication of making ISPs into utilities that not many people seem to talk about is the aspect of whether or not ISPs will be "protected carriers." A protected carrier is a legal designation for a company/service where the law recognizes that the company providing said service is only carrying goods from A to B, and does not create any packages or examine the contents of any package. It's why, if you ordered drugs online and got caught, your mailman wouldn't get slapped with drug-related criminal charges. Or why, if I sent a letter through California that didn't use someone's made up pronouns, the truck driver wouldn't get charged with hate speech. The government realizes the post office just delivers letters and boxes, and it would be impractical to make sure everything was legal at every point along the delivery route.

ISPs are currently, effectively, protected carriers. They literally just deliver data packets from A to B, and aren't supposed to inspect them. If they were to start looking at whether you're using Facebook or watching Netflix, that should, in theory, mean they are no longer a protected carrier. They'd then open themselves to being liable for any kiddie porn or death threats against Trump that their infrastructure was used to transmit. As I understand it, they seem to want the best of both being a protected carrier and not being one. I would too, if I were them, but I think being a "protected carrier" or not is a fairly sound way to handle the legalities of being a carrier of massive amounts of packages: You can either deliver them blindly, not examining the contents, and not be responsible for the contents, or alternatively, you can examine the contents of the packages and open yourself to liability for them.
